utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: Good afternoon to the Committee on Mental Health and Substance Use and to our chair.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: My name is Anne-Marie Foster, the president and CEO of Phoenix House of New York and Long Island.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: I am submitting the following testimony for the council's oversight hearing, syringe litter management, and related support.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: Since 1967, Phoenix House has been around helping thousands of individuals overcome substance use and alcohol use in order to lead healthy and productive, rewarding lives.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: Phoenix House offers a variety of behavioral health services for those with co-occurring mental health disorders, substance use disorders, and that includes residential services, outpatient service, recovery services, impaired driver programs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: And our services are designed to meet the individual needs of adults at various stages of their recovery, and that includes our veterans.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: Phoenix House also additionally provides educational and supportive services to the family members, friends, and significant others, and those in the community.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: And so with Phoenix House working on the front lines of the substance use and mental health crisis, I urge the committee to advance the council member.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: Carr's introduction bill of 0067-2026 to a full council vote, and I am testifying in support of council members'leads, resolutions 262 and 263.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: According to the New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene, and we heard them speak earlier, 2,192 residents died from an overdose in 2024, and black and Latino New Yorkers died of an overdose rate about twice that of white New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: And recent data and news tell us that this crisis is far from over.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: About a week and a half ago, prosecutors indicted two suspects for fatally dosing two New York City college students with fentanyl.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: Fentanyl test strips can accurately identify the presence of fentanyl in drugs and help individuals spot danger from an overdose.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: But test strips only save lives when people know they exist and where to get them and how to use them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: And Councilmember Carr's bill would require DOH and MH to develop an ongoing public health campaign that does exactly that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: This matters most for community members living in neighborhoods hit hardest, where trusted, accessible outreach and education is often out of reach at times.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: Passing this legislation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: Represents a crucial opportunity to help close the gap and arm New Yorkers with the tools they need to protect themselves and their neighbors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: I would also share that there is a cost-effective and efficient means to bring these services to neighborhoods that are hardest hit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: Something we did during the COVID, the dark days of our COVID pandemic.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: For those communities that were testing and vaccine resistant, the city brought the services to the communities by way of mobile vans.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: We have an opportunity to do just that with fentanyl test strips, naloxone, and recovery services, and collect syringes in these vans.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: With opioid settlement dollars, Phoenix House received their first mobile unit about earlier this summer, July.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: The first of its kind, and we would love to see this expanded citywide.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: Her name is Phoebe, Phoebe Phoenix.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: Phoenix House also has a Narcan and fentanyl test strip vending machine in Long Island City adjacent to our residential program across from Rainey Park.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: It is used quite frequently and we have to fill it up.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: Councilmember Lee's resolutions are another welcome part of a multifaceted addiction treatment and overdose prevention strategy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: Many people with substance use disorder first encounter the health care system through a primary care office, an ER, a specialist, rather than a treatment program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: And so what happens in that first encounter shapes whether they are recognized, treated with dignity, and connected to care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: Yet too many physicians finish medical school with little or no formal training in identifying treatment, treating addiction.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: Resolution 262 and 263 call on New York State and the federal government to require

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: addiction treatment training at medical schools that receive public funding.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: This is a reasonable condition for public dollars.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: It would help ensure that the next generation of doctors can better recognize substance use disorders, reduce stigma, offer evidence-based treatments such as medication for opiate use disorder, and make timely referrals to providers like Phoenix House.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: Earlier, better informed intervention means fewer people reaching crisis and fewer syringes, overdoses, and emergency calls on our streets and in our hospitals.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: Now more than ever, New York City needs to deploy every available tool.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: The health and the future of our community depend on what we do now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: Prevention, education, better trained health workforce all help accomplish this and allows providers like Phoenix House to save more lives.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: So I urge the committee to advance an introduction bill 007 to a...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: 2-6 and to support resolution 2-6 and 2-3.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: But I'd be remiss if I left this hearing and not say that distributing Narcan and fentanyl test strips is the floor.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: We can rescue people in the city all day long.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: We'd love to shift the conversation for how we help people live a life of recovery.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: Thank you for considering my testimony.

utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.text: I'd love to come visit Phoebe.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: Actually, we want to do a ride-along with Phoebe.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: I would be so down.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.text: I have a follow-up question.

utterances.text: Obviously, y'all are doing incredible work.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: you to do that work, you know, the Bronx and Queens, like there's an outsized impact and that's not reflected in the resources that especially Queens receive.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: As I said in my testimony, we have to bring the services to the people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: We know the hot spots.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: And I heard your question earlier when you talked about law enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: There is a shift with some of our law enforcement agencies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: I work very closely with the DEA, and they're on the record as saying that we're not going to law enforcement our way out of this problem.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: And so in collaboration, we were trying to figure out the funding that they go in and they do an action or they take down what they call the bad actors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: What are we replacing it with?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: All we're doing is two things.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: One, the community has been relying on that drug dealer is now susceptible to someone else coming in and bringing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: And we know our drug supply is tainted with fentanyl and the risk of overdoses going up in that community.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: We would love to see that in partnership, we now show up there, as I said, similar to what we did with COVID.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: When people in communities did not want to take the vaccine, we had vaccine equity issues.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: We knew the areas where those problems were, and we dispatched that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: We need to do the exact same thing with substance use.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: We can have the brick and mortar buildings, but there's going to be a subset of our population, just left the hearing earlier where we're talking about homelessness, that are not going to come out.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: not going to walk into our buildings, so we need to go to them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: And when we're going to them, not only are we going with Narcan, fentanyl test strips, and recovery coaching, we're going with food, we're going with a warm coat.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: And so we're building trust in the community and they get to rely on us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne-Marie Foster
utterances.text: And then we can move those individuals into our treatment facilities or any of the other treatment facilities that exist in the city.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Well, a reminder for nonprofits who are contracted to do business with the city is that these are capital projects that you can, like the vans are capital.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And I just, I encourage organizations to make those capital requests of all of us in the council.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: I feel like we don't, I feel like we don't get enough of them.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And to your point on the enforcement too, it's like, yeah, you have these big actions at the federal level and then what fills that void.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And then also sometimes you have the over-enforcement of low level where you're picking up somebody from a corner who's dealing a little bit just to support their own use and you're just replacing the person on the way.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And that's not doing us any good either.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: So it makes a ton of sense.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Well, anything else you'd like to add that you didn't say?

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: I mean, the floor is yours.
